# Native frame fixture provenance

`../oracle_frames.rs` contains 14 output vectors measured on 2026-11-13 from
the exact supplied ARM64 Android `liborbwebm2m.so`:

- SHA-256: `0e2fe6bf2987424e5f276f820aaf71d3b2292079136f3872f3e13337b6fb22eb`
- ELF build ID: `72b044850d9ce09ab49589a61d0a02e36f52e9a2`
- Export invoked: `CBasePacket::CBasePacket(int, int, const char*)` at `0x14dbe0`.
- Output obtained using `getRawPacketPtr` and `getRawPacketLength`, then destructor.

Inputs were generated by the test harness: command `7`, payload byte at index
`i` equal to `(17*i+3) mod 256`, and lengths
`0,1,4,5,8,15,16,17,31,32,33,255,256,513`. Command `7` was used to exercise the
generic packet constructor; arbitrary-length payloads here are **not** claims
that valid channel-open messages have those lengths.

The fixtures contain no camera addresses, account identifiers, credentials,
video, or packet captures. They record outputs for synthetic inputs, rather
than copying proprietary implementation code. The proprietary library and
Android runtime remain outside this crate.

Private investigation sources (not prerequisites to run these Rust tests):
`private-analysis/oracle-20261113/oracle.c`, `Dockerfile`, and `vectors.jsonl`.
Only records whose `kind` is `frame` were transferred into this test. Crypto
records in that private JSONL are outside this test's scope.

Exact oracle execution:

```sh
ssh RESEARCH_HOST 'docker run --rm --name motorola-offline-oracle --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --memory 256m --cpus 1 --pids-limit 32 local/motorola-offline-oracle:20261113' > private-analysis/oracle-20261113/vectors.jsonl 2>run.stderr
```

The image's executable command was:

```sh
qemu-aarch64 -E LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/runtime /runtime/linker64 /work/oracle /work/liborbwebm2m.so
```

The parent investigator observed exit status `0`; stderr only reported missing
Android generated linker configuration. No account/session/controller/camera
API was initialized. The container had no network connectivity and a read-only
filesystem. Library primitives were invoked offline through their exported ABI.

The Rust tests check byte-exact encoding, decoding at every split position,
and decoding of all measured frames coalesced into one input buffer. This
validates framing compatibility for these 14 inputs; it does not validate
session negotiation, encryption, transport, or reception of live video.
